raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fix residual replay running before FSDP gathers weights (#7777). With `residual_stream_recompute_num_layers=1`, finalize inside the owning layer; Shortcut-MoE pairs stay together.

Validation: 51 tests passed per rank on two GPUs, including a real MFSDP regression that reproduces the failure on the base revision. Eight four-GPU cases were not run. Formatting checks pass; Mypy diagnostics match the base.

On 72 GPUs, `num_layers=1`:

- **Versus replay disabled:** saves **10.31 GiB (7.82%)** of peak decoder memory per GPU for **2.18% more policy time**, measured over 100-update runs.
- **Versus `num_layers=4`:** uses **2.83 GiB more memory** for **8.3% less policy time**, from an earlier 64-update comparison that also coarsened FSDP boundaries.

[Evaluation details](http://nv/m7J).

- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.
- [x] I have included relevant unit tests.
- [x] I have documented the replay boundary and activation-memory tradeoff.

Thanks, @wujingyue, for the fix! Moving finalization inside the owning layer makes sense for `residual_stream_recompute_num_layers=1`, so the owner gathers its parameters before replay starts.

For memory-constrained workloads, we also want larger replay regions to retain fewer wide activation boundaries. As discussed in [my reply on #7777](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/7777#issuecomment-6368323687), we plan to address replay across multiple FSDP owners in follow-up PRs in the WR/mHC unification series tracked in [#7888](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/7888). The planned approach uses differentiable snapshots of the small WR controller and normalization parameters needed for replay, with correctness and memory/runtime validation under MFSDP.

Thanks also for pointing out the limitations of existing tests. I see the gap. The test over-specifies the internal call order without exercising backward or verifying the intended memory savings. We’ll address this in a separate test-only PR, replacing those brittle assertions with eager/replay backward parity and checks that intermediate activations are actually discarded and restored. Your change to execute the real Mamba forward already improves that coverage.

I'm not too happy with these test changes. The existing tests seem to be mocked up so much that it verifies implementation rather than user observable behavior. This makes the tests fragile. However, I don't have a great solution around.

+def test_residual_recompute_matches_eager_training(process_group_collection, distributed_setup):
+    """Per-layer residual replay must use weights gathered by the owning FSDP unit."""
+    if distributed_setup.world_size < 2:
+        pytest.skip("This test requires at least 2 ranks.")
+
+    config = TransformerConfig(
+        num_layers=2,
+        hidden_size=16,
+        num_attention_heads=4,
+        ffn_hidden_size=32,
+        attention_dropout=0.0,
+        hidden_dropout=0.0,
+        gradient_accumulation_fusion=False,
+        use_cpu_initialization=True,
+        wide_residual=WideResidualConfig(num_streams=3, streamwise_sigmoid_init_scale=0.01),
+    )
+    replay_config = replace(
+        config,
+        recompute_granularity="selective",
+        recompute_modules=["residual_stream"],
+        residual_stream_recompute_num_layers=1,
+    )
+    submodules = HybridStackSubmodules(
+        attention_layer=replace(get_gpt_layer_local_spec(), module=WideResidualTransformerLayer)
+    )
+    torch.manual_seed(1234)
+    reference, replay = [
+        HybridStack(
+            model_config,
+            submodules,
+            layer_type_list=[Symbols.ATTENTION] * config.num_layers,
+            post_layer_norm=False,
+            pg_collection=process_group_collection,
+        ).cuda()
+        for model_config in (config, replay_config)
+    ]
+    replay.load_state_dict(reference.state_dict())
+    replay = FullyShardedDataParallel(
+        config=replay_config,
+        ddp_config=DistributedDataParallelConfig(
+            use_megatron_fsdp=True,
+            megatron_fsdp_version=2,
+            use_distributed_optimizer=False,
+            data_parallel_sharding_strategy="optim_grads_params",
+            # Gather on demand so prefetch cannot hide replay before its owner.
+            suggested_communication_unit_size=0,
+        ),
+        module=replay,
+        pg_collection=process_group_collection,
+    )
+    assert all(isinstance(layer, FsdpModule) for layer in replay.module.layers)
+    reference_optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(reference.parameters(), lr=0.01)
+    replay_optimizer = get_megatron_optimizer(
+        OptimizerConfig(
+            optimizer="sgd", lr=0.01, sgd_momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0, clip_grad=0.0
+        ),
+        [replay],
+    )
+    # Identical inputs on every rank make averaged FSDP gradients match eager gradients.
+    inputs = torch.randn(4, 2, config.hidden_size, device="cuda")
+
+    def train(model, optimizer):
+        outputs, input_gradients = [], []
+        for _ in range(3):
+            optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
+            hidden = inputs.detach().clone().requires_grad_(True)
+
+            def forward():
+                output = model(hidden_states=hidden, attention_mask=None)
+                outputs.append(output.detach())
+                return output.square().mean()
+
+            run_forward_backward_on_microbatches(model, forward)
+            input_gradients.append(hidden.grad.detach().clone())
+            optimizer.step()
+        return torch.stack(outputs), torch.stack(input_gradients)
+
+    expected_outputs, expected_gradients = train(reference, reference_optimizer)
+    outputs, gradients = train(replay, replay_optimizer)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(outputs, expected_outputs)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(gradients, expected_gradients)
+
